title: The Complete Budget System That Actually Works
description:
Most budgets fail within weeks, and it's usually the system, not you. In this video I look at budgeting from three angles: the numbers (where the average household's $77,000 goes, the 50/30/20 rule, and the subscription leak most people underestimate by more than half), the 5 reasons your brain fights your budget, and a 12-step four-account system you can set up in one weekend.

Get The Ryan Rover Money Playbook: [LINK HERE]

1:25 How we got the numbers
1:55 Angle 1: The Numbers

8:40 The mindset that makes budgets stick

10:09 Step 2. Calculate your true monthly costs
11:06 Step 3. Choose your framework
11:57 Step 4. Set up four accounts
12:57 Step 5. Automate the payday flow
13:43 Step 6. Use a weekly spending number
14:26 Step 7. Build sinking funds
15:09 Step 8. Build your emergency fund
15:52 Step 9. Do a ten minute weekly check
16:27 Step 10. Hold a monthly money meeting
17:09 Step 11. Handle overspending without guilt
17:45 Step 12. Do an annual reset
18:24 A short history of budgeting
19:37 A quick favor
19:48 The system at three incomes
22:01 Two budgeters
23:18 Budgeting with irregular income
24:10 Budgeting as a couple
24:44 Apps, spreadsheets or envelopes?
25:15 Where to find money, category by category
27:17 Common budgeting mistakes
28:11 Tom's first year
28:54 Already budgeting?
29:21 Your setup weekend
29:49 But Ryan, what about...
30:36 Questions people ask
32:57 Recap: the 12 steps
34:14 What to do next

Sources:
- U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics, Consumer Expenditure Survey 2023 (average household spending and shares)
- Elizabeth Warren and Amelia Warren Tyagi, All Your Worth (2005), the 50/30/20 rule
- C+R Research, subscription spending survey (2022)
- Janet Polivy and C. Peter Herman, research on dieting and disinhibition (the what-the-hell effect)
- Richard H. Thaler, Mental Accounting Matters, Journal of Behavioral Decision Making (1999)
- IRS, estimated taxes for self-employed workers
